title: South Side clubs then and now
summary: Compared with today, there were many South Side clubs and taverns where musicians worked, but disc jockeys have removed the jobs.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Compared to today, the musicians on the South Side did have some clubs. They didn't play much money, but they had places to work, and today they don't have any places because of the disc jockey that come into the scene and he took the jobs away from them, and then the proprietor don't want -- after not paying musicians, you can't re-educate them to pay them now.

But back then, those days, they had all kinds of clubs, like the Delisa had a club and you had all kinds of taverns, and Swingland and all that. Just had a lot of places, all over the city, on the South Side, where you could work. And so the musicians were pretty much taken care of. But today it's a pitiful --
